cards.title: The published split leaks
cards.headline: 229/274 published test images (83.6 %) share an original photo with published train (97.1 % share a capture burst). A clean burst-level split drops macro F1 from 0.913 to 0.852.

numbers.label: macro F1, as distributed (published split, duplicates kept)
macro F1, published split, full image
macro F1, burst-level split, masked crop (ours)

cards.caveat: Leakage inflates macro F1 by a few points and the intervals overlap. insect_hole F1 near 1.00 in every arm is not credible as hole detection on its own: most hole photos come from sessions with no other class (see the session control).

cards.title: Per-class accuracy, within each dataset
cards.headline: On a clean split, broken vs sound reaches F1 0.820 on soybean (132 test seeds, 19 bursts) and macro F1 0.907 on Lin's four classes.
cards.caveat: Soybean test has only 19 independent bursts, so intervals are wide. Errors are mostly sound seeds called broken.

cards.title: Is hole detection real? Session control
cards.headline: On the only days with both holes and sound seeds, hole F1 is 0.975; a model that never saw a hole from those days still finds them (F1 0.962).

numbers.label: hole F1, same days and background
hole F1, trained on other sessions only

cards.caveat: Features do encode the capture session. With 7 hole bursts this is indicative, not conclusive.

cards.title: A model can tell which dataset a seed came from
cards.headline: A probe tells soybean d97rjyk2tz from Lin with 100 % accuracy on sound seeds, also from a texture-only central patch (100 %). Pooled class shares are uncalibrated on a new camera setup.

numbers.label: Lin sound seeds flagged defective by the pooled model

cards.caveat: Per-class numbers are reported within each dataset; a pooled model is not evidence of defect recognition across setups.

cards.title: Another setup's data does not replace local labels
cards.headline: On Lin, 10 local labels per class alone reach macro F1 0.89, against 0.68 for ~1,000 soybean images plus the same 10 labels.
cards.caveat: Mean over 10 random draws. Part of the drop is label shift: Lin 'broken' includes skin damage, soybean 'broken' is testa cracking. For a new crop or camera, budget for labelled target data.

cards.title: Counting seeds on real farmer photos
cards.headline: On Ghana phone photos (sun and hard shadow), our training-free segmenter is off by 1.7 seeds on average (1.1 %) against the 7 complete published counts.

numbers.label: % error vs semi-automatic estimate (105 photos, not ground truth)

cards.caveat: Only 7 photos have complete published counts, all FarmerSaved/Favor and mostly in sun. Failure modes: seeds cut by the photo border, dark table edges, single seeds counted as two.

cards.title: Lot-level % crushed: right for the wrong reasons
cards.headline: On 6 held-out harvest lots the % crushed is off by 1.5 points on average, but per-seed crushed F1 is only 0.478: errors cancel near 8 % prevalence.

numbers.label: true % inside the raw Wilson interval (sampling error only)
lots at an illustrative 5 % threshold (raw Wilson)

cards.caveat: Intervals are raw Wilson: they cover sampling error only, not classifier bias. Per-seed crushed F1 is only 0.48, so the accurate lot % comes from errors cancelling. Oracle segmentation (the dataset's own masks): this measures classification only. On a clean lot the same classifier would report a few % crushed. Show both sampling error and classifier bias, and say 'inconclusive' when the interval straddles the threshold.

cards.title: Robustness to image quality
cards.headline: Seed counts are stable (1 of 7 counts changed), but class shares move by 5.5 pp on average (up to 10.3 pp) when the same photo is downscaled and re-compressed.

numbers.label: count error vs published count, mean (seeds)
defect share change after re-compression, mean (pp)

cards.caveat: Class shares on Ghana photos are uncalibrated: this camera setup was never seen in training. Re-compression = downscale to 2000 px and save as JPEG quality 95.
